facts.statement: The only known fossil of Eoplesiosaurus is a single complete and articulated postcranial skeleton designated as holotype TTNCM 8348.
facts.quote: Eoplesiosaurus is known only from the holotype specimen TTNCM 8348, a complete and articulated postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected at Watchet in Somerset from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected at Watchet, of Somerset, from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation of the Lower Lias Group.

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus lived approximately 199.6 to 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage, just after the Triassic-Jurassic boundary.
facts.quote: Thus, they probably fall within the earliest Hettangian P. tilmanni Chronozone, which is about 199.6-198 million years old, immediately following the Triassic–Jurassic Boundary.

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus is considered one of the oldest known plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Hence, Eoplesiosaurus is one of the oldest plesiosaurs, to date.

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus was first described and named by Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans, and Patrick S. Druckenmiller in 2012.
facts.quote: Eoplesiosaurus was first described and named by Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans and Patrick S. Druckenmiller in 2012

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus had a proportionally long neck with at least 38 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Eoplesiosaurus is a proportionally long-necked plesiosaurian with at least 38 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 2012 phylogenetic analysis identified Eoplesiosaurus as the most basal known plesiosauroid.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Benson et al. (2012) found it to be the basalmost known plesiosauroid.

facts.statement: A later analysis by Benson & Druckenmiller (2014) placed Eoplesiosaurus as a basal plesiosaur outside the group Plesiosauroidea.
facts.quote: However, an analysis performed by Benson & Druckenmiller (2014) found it as a basal plesiosaur, outside of Plesiosauroidea.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected in Street, Watchet, Somerset, from the Pre-Planorbis beds of the Blue Lias Formation.
facts.quote: Fue recolectado en Street, en Watchet en Somerset, en los lechos de Pre-Planorbis de la Formación Blue Lias del Grupo Lias Inferior.

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus is a plesiosaur with a proportionally long neck containing at least 38 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Eoplesiosaurus es un plesiosaurio con un cuello proporcionalmente largo con al menos 38 vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: Small conical lateral projections on the bases of the anterior cervical prezygapophyses represent the autapomorphy of Eoplesiosaurus.
facts.quote: La presencia de pequeñas proyecciones cónicas laterales en las bases de las prezigapófisis cervicales anteriores representan su autapomorfia.

facts.statement: Eoplesiosaurus was originally described and named by Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans, and Patrick S. Druckenmiller in 2012.
facts.quote: Eoplesiosaurus fue descrito y nombrado originalmente por Roger B. J. Benson, Mark Evans y Patrick S. Druckenmiller en 2012

facts.statement: The genus name Eoplesiosaurus is derived from the Greek word for 'dawn' combined with Plesiosaurus, referencing its elongated neck.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del griego Eo, "amanecer" añadido a Plesiosaurus en referencia a su cuello alargado, también presente en Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: The species name antiquior is derived from a Latin term meaning 'most ancient', referring to the specimen's geological age and the painting Duria Antiquior.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del término que en latín significa "antiquísimo", por la antigüedad geológica del espécimen y también por la pintura conocida como Duria Antiquior

facts.statement: The time range for Eoplesiosaurus is recorded as the Hettangian stage, from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Hettangian (201.4 to 199.5 million years ago)
